subject: Elon Musk's 2016 public statements about Tesla Autopilot
called_fake_by: Tesla's lawyers, in a wrongful-death lawsuit
claim: Lawyers for the family of a man killed using Autopilot wanted to question Musk about his 2016 claims. Tesla's lawyers argued it couldn't confirm the recordings were genuine because Musk is a frequent deepfake target.
finding: No one presented evidence that the recordings were altered. The judge called the argument deeply troubling: it would let famous people disown anything they said on record.
outcome: The judge rejected the argument and tentatively ordered Musk to sit for a deposition.

sources.title: People are trying to claim real videos are deepfakes. The courts are not amused
Elon Musk will likely testify about his Autopilot statements
